question.text: Two solids <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> respectively are moving with equal linear momentum. The ratio of their kinetic energies <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mfenced><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>.</mo><mi>E</mi><mo>.</mo></mrow></mfenced><mi>A</mi></msub><mo>:</mo><msub><mfenced><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>.</mo><mi>E</mi><mo>.</mo></mrow></mfenced><mi>B</mi></msub></math> will be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo></math> so the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> will be _________.
